levels.name: Mia, 22, Intern
levels.story: The 8 levels of midnight symptom googling. Level 1. Level 1: 42 searched symptoms at 3:17 AM and zero medical degrees. My forehead number glows a terrifying forty-two, meaning forty-two unread web pages telling me I am dying of a rare tropical parasite that eats human brain tissue from the inside out within forty-eight hours. I stare at my cheap phone screen in my dark studio apartment, tears stinging my eyes while my chest heaves with uncontrolled spasms. A tiny golden coin gleams right beside my half-empty mug of tap water. You are keeping the whole floor awake with your pathetic hypochondria again, you fragile little brat! I clutch my chest, struggling for oxygen, and whisper back through the door frame. I cannot breathe, my resting heart rate is one hundred and forty, I need an ambulance right now! You just need to sleep off your fake diseases, nobody cares if you drop dead tonight. Then she typed the exact phrase that made my blood run ice cold. You'll see that in Level 2.

levels.name: Leo, 28, Barista
levels.story: The 8 levels of midnight symptom googling. Level 2. Level 2: 12 open browser tabs on a cracked laptop while my forehead glows a stubborn twelve. I am convinced my left eyelid twitch means a neurological shutdown and permanent paralysis before dawn. A tiny golden coin rests right on top of my espresso tamper. My coworker Broccoli Ben strides past the counter, grabs my laptop, and decides to humiliate me in front of all the early morning customers standing in line. Listen up everybody, our dear barista Leo is researching stage four brain tumors because his left eye twitched twice! I wipe cold sweat from my forehead and glare back at him with absolute fury. My pulse is dangerously irregular, Ben, I can feel it pounding in my teeth, stop mocking me! You are just hungover from cheap energy drinks after crying over Mia's forty-two symptoms, stop wasting time and pour my macchiato. Then the store manager walked in and whispered these chilling words. You'll see that in Level 3.

levels.name: Maya, 31, Accountant
levels.story: The 8 levels of midnight symptom googling. Level 3. Level 3: 3 AM forum rabbit holes where every headache is a stroke and every blurry vision means total blindness. My forehead glows the number three representing three consecutive hours spent reading obscure medical blogs while listening to Leo's barista breakdown. A tiny golden coin gleams beside my spreadsheet calculator. An arrogant voice cuts through the quiet office kitchenette as Lemon Luke saunters in. You are wasting sick days on internet self-diagnoses again, Maya, just like that fragile intern Mia and that hysterical barista Leo! I grip my desk calendar so hard my knuckles turn white and I stare him down with pure hatred. My left arm feels completely numb, Luke, this is not normal, I am having a cardiac event! You just cannot handle tax season pressure, deal with your pathetic delusions yourself. Then my phone buzzed with an automated notification from the hospital portal. You'll see that in Level 4.

levels.name: Pam
levels.story: The 8 levels of midnight symptom googling. Level 4. Level 4: 1,200 dollars in out-of-pocket urgent care bills because Google told me my strange skin rash was a flesh-eating tropical disease. My forehead glows the exact deductible amount for my MRI scan. A tiny golden coin rests on top of my rejected claim forms. Suddenly, my office intercom buzzes and CEO Coconut Coco's cold corporate voice echoes through the room. Your policy does not cover midnight panic searches or hypochondriac emergency visits, Pam, so pay your own bills! I slam my approval stamp down on the desk in pure rage, knocking over my coffee, and shout back into the speaker. I cannot sleep, my entire left side is tingling just like Maya and Mia reported, and you are going to authorize this MRI right now! Pay your own deductible or stop calling us at 4 AM with your childish meltdowns. Then my personal phone received an unknown caller ID. You'll see that in Level 5.

levels.name: Sam, 29, ER Nurse
levels.story: The 8 levels of midnight symptom googling. Level 5. Level 5: 4 hours of total sleep after a double shift spent reassuring patients like Pam and Leo who googled their headaches. My forehead glows the pathetic number four representing my nightly rest. A tiny golden coin gleams beside my triage clipboard. An exhausted accountant bursts through the trauma doorway and it is Maya, glaring at me with pure contempt. Stop complaining about exhaustion when you triage us for minor panic attacks, Sam, my arm is numb and you are ignoring me! I lean against the nurse station desk, rubbing my temples, and sigh deeply as my anger boils over. I have been on my feet for fourteen hours straight dealing with your internet self-diagnoses, Maya! We all have deadlines and insurance denials like Pam, deal with your own fatigue and get out of my triage bay! Then the head physician walked past me and dropped a heavy manila folder. You'll see that in Level 6.
